title: Service Capacity Assurance: Performance Matrix, Error‑Budget Modeling, and Escalation Procedures
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a contract-ready appendix and internal runbook that defines: 1) a compact performance assurance matrix that maps committed throughput bands to measurable SLOs and allowable degradation windows; 2) a transparent error‑budget modeling approach for credit calculations; and 3) a staged escalation and remediation procedure tailored for Dedicated customers. This ticket produces text approved for inclusion in the dedicated capacity addendum and the internal ops runbook for on-call and account teams.
measurement_method: SLO measurement uses a rolling 30-day window unless otherwise noted; weighted per-tenant when a reservation spans multiple AZs. Throughput computed from accepted request completions with agreed routing headers. Metrics derived from Console per-route telemetry and billing reconciliation exports.
error_budget_definition: Error budget is defined as the allowed percent of committed throughput not met within the measurement window. For a commitment C tokens/min (or requests/min), monthly error_budget = max(0, C * measurement_window_minutes - actual_serves). We convert shortfalls to a percentage of the committed capacity for credit tiers.
credit_formula: Credits are computed using a two-part model: (A) proportional shortfall credit = (shortfall_percent_of_commit * monthly_fee * proportionality_factor) and (B) service-level credit cap = min(proportional_credit, cap_pct_of_monthly_fee). Example: For shortfall 10%, proportionality_factor=0.8 -> credit = 8% of monthly fee; cap_pct_of_monthly_fee=40% prevents runaway credits.
credit_schedule: Tiered schedule by shortfall bands with decreasing remediation obligations: 0-2% no credit; 2-10% Tier 1 credit (proportional); 10-25% Tier 2 credit + mandatory partner review and optional one-time capacity uplift; >25% Tier 3 credit, expedited remediation, and optional right-to-terminate notice. Credits applied to next invoice unless customer requests immediate one-off reimbursement.
autoscale_policy_summary: Autoscaling controlled by customer-configurable policy and Redwood floor protections. Policy knobs: target_utilization (70-85%), burst_buffer_seconds, warm_pool_reserve_fraction. In contract appendix we surface guaranteed autoscale response: 'Redwood will aim to add reserved capacity within X minutes for sustained uplifts above Y% of commit for Z minutes' with explicit burst limits. Autoscale failure modes and fallback (throttle to best-effort lane / route to compatible lower-capacity model variant) are documented.
fleet_controls: Fleet controls include per-customer AZ spread requirements, minimum warm-pool nodes, deploy freeze windows, and prioritized routing for ticketed incidents. Controls allow Redwood to pin customer workloads to an isolated pool for high-sensitivity customers and to enable graceful degradation policies (percent-based shedding by non-essential routes). All controls are configurable via Dedicated Console and exposed in the addendum as options with cost deltas.
risks: Credit model may undercompensate for tail latency-driven user-visible failures
Measurement drift between telemetry and billing data requires reconciliation pipeline
Autoscale cold-starts on certain instance types could lengthen remediation times
open_questions: Legal: acceptability of cap_pct default of 40% for enterprise contracts?
Ops: can we guarantee 'add reserved capacity within X minutes' for all regions or must this be region-specific?
Billing: should credits be automated or require customer opt-in to apply against next invoice?
